The river in winter

By A. Writer

Every winter the river freezes from its banks inwards, and for a few weeks the town walks on it. The ice is thickest near the old mill, where the water runs slowest.

Nobody remembers who first crossed it on foot, but the town keeps a record of the days it was safe, and it has been getting shorter for thirty years.

We used to skate to school.
